{{short description|American origami artist (born 1960)}}
[[Image:Montroll Origami Tyrannosaurus.jpg|thumb|An origami Tyrannosaurus folded from Montroll's instructions]]
'''John Montroll''' (born January 1, 1960) is an [[Americans|American]] [[origami]] artist, author, teacher, and mathematician. He has written many books on origami, promoting the single-square, no-cut, no glue approach. Montroll taught mathematics at [[St. Anselm's Abbey School]] in [[Washington, D.C.]] from 1990 to 2021.

==Biography==

John Montroll was born in [[Washington, D.C.]]<ref name=biopage>The Origamian, Vol.9, Issue 3, 1970, Published by the Origami Center</ref> He is the son of [[Elliott Waters Montroll]], an American scientist and mathematician. He has a [[Bachelor of Arts]] degree in Mathematics from the [[University of Rochester]], a [[Master of Arts]] in [[Electrical Engineering]] from the [[University of Michigan]], and a Master of Arts in [[applied mathematics]] from the [[University of Maryland]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.saintanselms.org/about_us/directory/jmontroll/index.aspx|title=Mr. John Montroll|website=[[St. Anselm's Abbey School]]|accessdate=March 24, 2015|archive-date=January 4, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170104091501/http://www.saintanselms.org/about_us/directory/jmontroll/index.aspx|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Montroll mastered his first origami book, Isao Honda's ''How to make Origami'', at the age of six,<ref name=biopage/> the same age he began creating his own origami animals.<ref name=interview1>The Paper, Issue 55, Summer 1996, The Magazine of [[OrigamiUSA]]</ref> He became a member of the [[Origami Center of America]] at age twelve.<ref name=biopage/>  He attended his first origami convention at age 14. In 2021, Montroll retired from his job at [[St. Anselm's Abbey School]] in Washington, D.C., where he taught [[mathematics]], as well as an origami class. One of John Montroll's hobbies is whistling. He claims to be able to whistle in five octaves and to have shown this talent at two whistling conventions in [[Louisburg, North Carolina]].<ref>{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110305105021/http://www.eorigamipublishing.com/home/montroll|url=http://www.eorigamipublishing.com/home/montroll|title=John Montroll|website=eOrigami Publishing|first=John|last=Montroll|url-status=dead|accessdate=July 7, 2023|archive-date=March 5, 2011}}</ref>

John Montroll pioneered modern origami with the publication of his first book, ''Origami for the Enthusiast''; Dover Publications, 1979, which was the first origami book where each model is folded from single square sheet and no cuts.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Dias|first1=Chryselle D’Silva|title=In the Fold -|url=http://www.home-review.com/2014/05/fold/|website=Home Review: In The Fold|publisher=Home Review Magazine}}</ref> In the same book he introduced the origami term "double rabbit ear fold."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.smashwords.com/profile/view/montrollorigami|title=John Montroll|accessdate=March 24, 2015|website=[[Smashwords]]}}</ref> He is also known for inventing the "dog base".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.britishorigami.org/cp-resource/origami-glossary/|title=Origami Glossary|website=British Origami|first=Nick|last=Robinson}}</ref> His work in the field of origami was briefly mentioned in the York series by author [[Laura Ruby]].
